newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Asahi Breweries profit up 45 percent.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Asahi Breweries profit up 45 percent.

text.p: Asahi Breweries Ltd. reported a 45 percent jump in profits Tuesday, a day after rival Kirin Brewery Co. Ltd said its profits and sales declined.

Asahi Breweries, Japan's second largest beer producer, said its parent current profit reached 18.17 billion yen ($155 million) in the first six months of its fiscal year, up 44.9 percent from a year ago.
"The profit rise is mainly because of robust sales of our beer," an Asahi spokesman said. Current profit is pretax income that includes gains and losses from non-operating activities.
Asahi said shipments of its mainstay brand, Super Dry, in the January-June period jumped 20 percent from a year ago.
Analysts said Super Dry's success was partly due to Asahi's emphasis on marketing the product to supermarkets and mass retailers rather than small liquor shops.
While Asahi enjoyed strong sales, industry leader Kirin Brewery's sales and earnings fell.
Kirin said Monday that its parent current profit declined to 25.3 billion yen ($215 million) from 27.5 billion yen ($235 million) a year ago.
Shipments of Kirin's mainstay Kirin Lager fell 11.7 percent from a year ago.
